topic:
Revival of banked downgraded parent stat_cate_local_overlap_nuisance_frontier (v1), targeting its exact-uniform bounded-overlap converse that remained open. This attempt uses a joint-cell correlated-prior construction and sparse latent-sign graph component control of the full fixed-n mixture likelihood. The parent already tried smooth overlapping frames; the new ingredient is the component affinity and random-geometric-graph bound that replaces the failed partition-local transfer. Resolve the same-class below-elbow minimax rate with a matching total estimator; the rate answer remains open for independent verification. The parent all-kappa oracle theorem and unmatched upper bracket alone do not discharge this kernel. MODEL: For every fixed d>=1, alpha>0, beta>0, gamma>beta, L>=4 with S=alpha+beta<d*gamma/(2*gamma+d), observe n>=2 iid (X,A,Y). X has exactly the known uniform law on [0,1]^d. A|X=x is Bernoulli(g(x)/4), with g in H^alpha(L), 1<=g<=2. Y|(X=x,A=a) is Bernoulli(mu_a(x)), mu0 in H^beta(L), tau=mu1-mu0 in H^gamma(L), and 1/8<=mu0,mu1<=7/8. H^s(L) bounds derivatives through m=ceil(s)-1 by L and the order-m derivatives have (s-m)-Holder seminorm <=L under the sup norm. No smoothness of the marginal outcome mean is assumed. The estimator knows d,alpha,beta,gamma,L and uniform design, but not g,mu0,tau. Target is the unique continuous version tau(0); conditional exchangeability and consistency provide the causal interpretation. This is precisely the parent kappa=0 subproblem, preserving its exact-support restriction. KERNEL: Determine the sharp order of R_n=inf_T sup_P E_P|T(O_1,...,O_n)-tau_P(0)| over all Borel data-only estimators on the exact model above, for every stated fixed parameter tuple and all n>=2. Deliver an explicit deterministic rate rho_n (including any logarithmic factors), constants 0<c<=C<infinity depending only on the fixed parameters, c*rho_n<=R_n<=C*rho_n, and a total finite computable attaining estimator. Resolve whether the published candidate n^(-1/(1+d/(2gamma)+d/(2S))) is sharp on exact uniform support or supply a sharper matched replacement; the answer is open, not imposed. Characterize when the same-class oracle benchmark n^(-gamma/(2gamma+d)) remains attainable in this below-published-elbow regime. The required lower bound must concern fixed-n iid product laws in this exact full-support Bernoulli class. A conditional or Poissonized proof must prove a valid reduction back to that experiment. COMPUTATION: Use the parent finite projection U-statistic/local polynomial estimator if its rate is matched; if the class yields a faster rate, give an explicit finite projection or higher-order correction estimator with deterministic tuning, singular-matrix fallback and clipping. Frame/likelihood calculations for a lower bound are proof mechanics, not model assumptions. CONSUMER: The parent names the grf causal_forest/R-learner workflow for estimating heterogeneous treatment effects from observational data with learned propensity/outcome regressions. This theorem tells users when nuisance learning imposes an unavoidable pointwise precision penalty even under benign known covariate design, or whether that penalty is avoidable. It is a precision benchmark, not a claim that existing forests attain it; no application is changed from the parent. PRIOR ART: The parent receipts say the published higher-order upper rate already applies to exact known uniform design, but the perforated-support lower laws do not. The target is the missing full-support fixed-n converse or a sharper matched same-class answer. Sparse latent-sign component control is the presolved replacement for the failed partition-local affinity argument; no new literature review is claimed. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The presolver derives a full-support Bernoulli lower family using a smooth squared partition of unity and correlated signs, with a deterministic macro contrast and exact one-observation mixture cancellation. Conditional on the observed covariates, connect observations whose local frames share a sign. Product mixtures factor over components, singleton components agree, and a mixed-derivative bound controls each remaining component by a²b² times a polynomial and exponential in its size. A spanning-tree count gives a total fixed-n squared Hellinger bound of order n² h^d ell^d a²b². Below the nuisance elbow, n ell^d is small at the proposed tuning, yielding the missing nuisance-rate converse without deleting support. Root separately checked rational cell normalization, shared-coefficient mixture leakage, disjoint-component cancellation, overlapping pair/triple examples, and unequal-smoothness rate exponents. These finite checks do not prove the analytic theorem.
UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Independently verify the smooth-frame support and Hölder estimates, component mixed-derivative constants, geometric-graph counting, and the inherited upper estimator; the presolver reports an analytic closure, not a certified theorem.
EARLY KILL TEST: On d=1, alpha=beta=1/8, gamma=1, verify the full fixed-n component factorization and affinity estimate at ell proportional to n^(-8/7); stop if an uncancelled singleton or macro-scale leakage term survives.
STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/mill/scratch/mill-w10/revival_cate_presolve_strongest.md.

open_problems.open_problem: For κ=0 and S=α+β<dγ/(2γ+d), determine whether the exact-uniform fixed-n pointwise-CATE minimax risk is of order n^{-1/(1+d/(2γ)+d/(2S))} or a faster matched rate.

source_refs.claim: The published nuisance-rate converse uses a density supported on perforated flat-top regions, while the role of the covariate density is left open.
source_refs.author: Edward H. Kennedy, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, James M. Robins, Larry Wasserman

source_refs.claim: Develops two-convex-mixture minimax lower bounds for functionals depending on multiple infinite-dimensional nuisances.
source_refs.author: James M. Robins, Eric Tchetgen Tchetgen, Lingling Li, Aad van der Vaart

source_refs.claim: Obtains a sharp nuisance-limited rate for an analogous random-design conditional-variance problem using local U-statistics and coupled least-favorable laws.
source_refs.author: Yandi Shen, Chao Gao, Daniela Witten, Fang Han

source_refs.excerpt: Below that elbow, claim only the proved bracket and leave the exact-uniform nuisance converse open.
Complete the exact-uniform bounded-overlap converse for α+β<dγ/(2γ+d)
overlapping smooth frames violate the partition-local premise

open_problems.why_unsolved: Kennedy et al.'s lower construction removes covariate mass from bump-transition regions, producing partition-local cancellation but leaving its hard laws outside the singleton exact-uniform class. Under full uniform support, disjoint nuisance-scale perturbations violate γ-Hölder regularity, overlapping smooth frames create shared-sign multi-observation likelihood terms, and filling the support holes leaves a first-order leakage term. The parent's total projection U-statistic upper bound therefore does not settle sharpness. The proposed correlated-sign component argument must still verify smooth-frame admissibility, singleton and macro-scale cancellation, component mixed-derivative constants, random-geometric-graph enumeration, and a fixed-n product-law affinity bound.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A resolution would give an explicit deterministic ρ_n, constants 0<c≤C depending only on the fixed parameters, and cρ_n≤R_n≤Cρ_n for all n≥2, with a legal full-support fixed-n Bernoulli mixture converse and a total finite attaining estimator.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its regression-versus-functional motivation and nuisance-elbow formulation while making exact full support the decisive proof boundary.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: A smooth pointwise CATE can be easier than its nuisance regressions -> higher-order localization predicts a below-elbow rate -> the published converse modifies covariate support -> exact uniform support requires a new fixed-n mixture argument

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the two-convex-mixture lower-bound theorem and product-experiment Hellinger calculation from independent partition cells to connected components of overlapping sign frames.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired converse must hide a target shift through coordinated perturbations of two nuisances, with component dependence replacing partition-local factorization.

method_exemplars.technique: Retain the localized finite-series higher-order R-learner and quadratic U-statistic bias-variance balance while replacing support deletion in the least-favorable experiment.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the candidate rate and closest attaining-estimator architecture, and its lower design identifies the precise support step that fails.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt its random-design local-polynomial U-statistic decomposition and coupled mixture control to bound non-singleton interactions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Conditional variance and pointwise CATE share the geometry of a smooth functional obscured by a rough regression nuisance under full random design.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct honest pointwise confidence intervals for τ(0) in the exact-uniform below-elbow Hölder CATE model whose worst-case expected length has the sharp minimax order.

source_refs.claim: The paper establishes point-risk bounds and lists distribution theory and inference for its minimax estimator as future work.
source_refs.author: Edward H. Kennedy, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, James M. Robins, Larry Wasserman

source_refs.claim: Provides doubly robust CATE confidence bands using first-order smoothing and parametric nuisance models, not the below-elbow higher-order Hölder regime.
source_refs.author: Sokbae Lee, Ryo Okui, Yoon-Jae Whang

open_problems.why_unsolved: Below the nuisance elbow, the localized quadratic correction may have a leading degenerate U-statistic component, its projection rank diverges, and smoothing bias is comparable to stochastic error. Consequently, neither the existing risk inequality nor first-order Gaussian CATE-band theory yields uniform coverage. A resolution must determine the correct normalization and limit law or construct a bias-aware non-Gaussian procedure while uniformly controlling projection, localization, and nuisance-training errors.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A resolution would construct intervals CI_n satisfying inf_P P_P{τ_P(0)∈CI_n}≥1−δ−o(1) with worst-case expected length of the sharp minimax order, supported by either a uniform studentized limit theorem or a finite-sample calibrated alternative.

writing_exemplar.why: Its discussion directly separates the solved minimax-risk question from the unresolved distributional and inferential problem.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: A minimax estimator quantifies achievable point precision -> scientific use requires uncertainty statements -> below-elbow higher-order corrections evade first-order CATE inference -> derive honest rate-optimal pointwise intervals

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt higher-order influence-function interval construction, truncated von Mises bias control, and U-statistic limit analysis.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The candidate point estimator is a localized higher-order influence-function estimator in a non-root-n, growing-projection regime.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt its Gaussian-process approximation and calibration of doubly robust smoothed CATE bands.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the closest CATE-specific coverage proof, with the first-order linearization replaced by a localized quadratic U-statistic analysis.

method_exemplars.technique: Use its pointwise centering, asymptotic-normality, and variance-estimation blueprint for an honest heterogeneous-effect learner.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It clarifies the coverage-facing deliverables needed to connect a minimax benchmark to practical pointwise CATE inference.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine the adaptation price for estimating τ(0) under exact uniform design when α, β, and γ are unknown, and construct a data-driven selector of localization bandwidth and projection rank across both sides of the nuisance elbow.

source_refs.claim: Its rate-optimal estimator uses smoothness-dependent deterministic bandwidth and projection dimension, and the paper leaves adaptivity and data-driven tuning open.
source_refs.author: Edward H. Kennedy, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, James M. Robins, Larry Wasserman

source_refs.claim: Proves adaptive upper and lower bounds using Lepski selection over finite-projection second-order U-statistics, but does not treat localized pointwise CATE.
source_refs.author: Lin Liu, Rajarshi Mukherjee, James M. Robins, Eric Tchetgen Tchetgen

open_problems.why_unsolved: The optimal bandwidth and projection rank depend jointly on three unknown smoothness indices and change their balance at the nuisance elbow. Standard one-parameter Lepski comparisons do not directly control a two-dimensional family of localized growing-rank U-statistics with learned nuisances. It is also unknown whether adaptation is free away from the elbow or necessarily incurs a logarithmic penalty at or across the transition, so a lower bound is needed to separate intrinsic adaptation cost from proof artifacts.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A resolution would give an explicit data-only selector over a finite deterministic (h,k) grid, an adaptive oracle inequality, and a matching constrained-risk lower bound over a stated union of Hölder classes, including every unavoidable logarithmic factor.

writing_exemplar.why: Its explicit smoothness-dependent tuning and phase transition provide the natural setup for the adaptation question.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Oracle tuning attains the smooth-class minimax rate -> nuisance and target smoothness are unknown in applications -> the optimal bandwidth-rank balance changes across the elbow -> characterize and attain the adaptive envelope

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt Lepski selection among finite-dimensional second-order U-statistic estimators together with its matching adaptive lower-bound argument.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The pointwise-CATE estimator has the same projection-plus-quadratic-U-statistic architecture, with localization adding a second tuning coordinate.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over the modified Lepski method designed for unavailable sharp tails of higher-order U-statistics and its constrained-risk lower bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The below-elbow selector faces the same higher-order concentration obstruction, compounded by pointwise localization and nuisance fitting.

method_exemplars.technique: Use its explicit decomposition of target bias, nuisance-product projection bias, linear variance, and degenerate U-statistic variance as the comparison scale.
method_exemplars.why_closest: That decomposition defines the oracle envelope the selector must recover without knowing α, β, or γ.

open_problems.open_problem: For κ>0, determine the complete pointwise-CATE minimax frontier under e(x)=||x||∞^κg(x)/4, including the oracle-attainment region, nuisance-dominated branches, critical logarithms, and matching total estimators.

source_refs.excerpt: The complete kappa>0 higher-order frontier is also open.
State and prove a first explicit nondegenerate κ>0 branch—upper and lower rate bracket included
higher-order upper and lower frontier, critical logarithms, and complete oracle-penalty classification remain open

open_problems.why_unsolved: The parent settles the supplied-propensity rate n^{-γ/(2γ+d+κ)} and a first-order data-only bracket, but bounded-overlap corrections do not transfer mechanically. On a shrinking corner neighborhood, treated Gram eigenvalues and effective sample size acquire h^κ factors while propensity, projection, and stabilization errors are amplified differently. Legal lower laws must additionally handle noninteger corner powers and max-norm tie surfaces without support deletion, so neither the bounded-overlap elbow nor α+β≥γ is known to be necessary for oracle attainment.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A resolution would give an explicit piecewise ρ_n(d,κ,α,β,γ,L), a total finite attaining estimator, matching fixed-n lower experiments, and exact inequalities characterizing when ρ_n is of order n^{-γ/(2γ+d+κ)}.

writing_exemplar.why: Use its oracle-versus-nuisance phase-diagram framing while replacing uniform positivity by a geometric propensity zero.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Pointwise CATE has oracle and nuisance difficulty -> orthogonal corrections create an elbow under bounded overlap -> local treatment scarcity changes every information balance -> characterize the new oracle-versus-unknown frontier

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt localized projection U-statistic corrections and rebalance approximation bias, projection bias, and degenerate variance with h^κ-weighted moments.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest sharp pointwise-CATE construction for the same asymmetric Hölder nuisance structure.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over local-mass normalization and regularly varying design calculations for the oracle component.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Conditionally treated observations near the corner form a degenerate local design with effective mass h^{d+κ}.

method_exemplars.technique: Use higher-order influence-function projection kernels to cancel successive products of propensity and outcome-regression errors.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The unknown-g penalty is generated by products of infinite-dimensional nuisance errors coupled to weak local overlap.

open_problems.open_problem: If the full-support correlated-sign component construction works under exact uniform design, determine whether it transfers to unknown covariate densities constrained only by 0<f_-≤f≤f_+ and resolves the positive-band pointwise-CATE minimax rate.

source_refs.excerpt: The exact positive-band minimax exponent, a matching converse ... remain open.
extend the close-pair upper bound off the alpha<=1, beta<alpha subregion
build the mixture handle from a smooth squared frame on the full uniform interval

open_problems.why_unsolved: The positive-band run proves close-pair achievability only in a restricted smoothness region, while its converse encounters the same transition-region leakage created by forbidding support holes. Component affinity could control overlapping frames, but the first proof step changes because cell masses, component edge probabilities, projection Grams, and mixture integrals are no longer deterministic Lebesgue quantities and must be bounded uniformly over an unknown, potentially nonsmooth density. The existing upper estimator also does not cover every nuisance ordering or smoothness above one.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A resolution would identify the sharp positive-band minimax rate, prove a uniform fixed-n component-mixture converse over all densities in [f_-,f_+], and match it with a total close-pair or empirical-projection estimator covering all α,β>0.

writing_exemplar.why: Retain its nuisance-elbow narrative while foregrounding whether the covariate-density class itself permits the lower experiment.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Higher-order CATE estimation predicts a nuisance branch -> the standard converse shapes covariate support -> a positive density band forbids that device -> determine the band-only minimax exponent

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt two-mixture Hellinger control after replacing deterministic partition probabilities by density-uniform component bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination still requires coordinated nuisance perturbations, but dependence is indexed by random overlapping-frame components.

method_exemplars.technique: Transfer random-design local U-statistic concentration and full-support mixture calculations.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its random-design functional problem directly handles nonuniform cell occupancy without a supplied projection Gram.

method_exemplars.technique: Use empirical projection kernels and matrix-perturbation bounds to avoid smoothness assumptions on the design density.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination estimator must replace the exact Lebesgue Gram matrix while preserving higher-order nuisance cancellation.

literature_map:
Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins, and Wasserman (2024, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:2203.00837) establish the pointwise Hölder-CATE nuisance elbow and a localized quadratic R-learner upper bound.
Their lower design is uniform only on a perforated set of flat bump tops plus the region away from the target; it is not the exact uniform design.
The same paper leaves covariate-density effects, estimator distribution theory, L2/L∞ risk, testing, adaptivity, and data-driven bandwidth/rank selection open.
Kennedy (2023, Electronic Journal of Statistics, arXiv:2004.14497) gives DR- and R-learner oracle inequalities and the precursor local-polynomial construction under bounded overlap.
Nie and Wager (2021, Biometrika, arXiv:1712.04912) establish quasi-oracle R-learning under sufficient nuisance control, not the rough-nuisance minimax frontier.
Robins, Li, Tchetgen Tchetgen, and van der Vaart (2008, arXiv:0805.3040) develop higher-order influence-function U-statistic estimators and interval methods.
Robins, Tchetgen Tchetgen, Li, and van der Vaart (2009, Electronic Journal of Statistics, DOI 10.1214/09-EJS479) provide the two-mixture minimax device used by later CATE lower bounds.
Shen, Gao, Witten, and Han (2020, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:1902.10822) solve an analogous random-design conditional-variance problem with local U-statistics and joint design/noise alternatives.
Liu, Mukherjee, Robins, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2021, JMLR, arXiv:1608.01364) obtain adaptive Lepski selection for finite-projection second-order U-statistics, but not localized CATE.
Lee, Okui, and Whang (2017, Journal of Applied Econometrics, arXiv:1601.02801) provide doubly robust CATE bands under first-order smoothing and parametric nuisance models.
Belloni, Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2015, Journal of Econometrics, arXiv:1212.0442) and Wager and Athey (2018, JASA, arXiv:1510.04342) supply adjacent uniform and pointwise Gaussian inference under regimes avoiding the below-elbow higher-order limit problem.
Gao and Han (2020, NeurIPS, arXiv:2002.06471) show that covariate geometry and density ratios can alter heterogeneous-effect minimax difficulty.
Crump, Hotz, Imbens, and Mitnik (2008, Review of Economics and Statistics, DOI 10.1162/rest.90.3.389) study tests of zero or constant CATE, while Bonvini, Kennedy, and Keele (2023, arXiv:2306.17464) study minimax benefit-set recovery.
The central tension is that known uniform design simplifies Gram construction and upper estimation but invalidates the support-deletion device used by the closest nuisance-rate converse.
Searches through September 2026 found no paper closing the exact-known-uniform fixed-n converse or deriving limit theory for the corresponding minimax estimator.
